title: Choose the Source Review workspace structure
question: Which composition should govern the first real application screen after a CSV is opened? The Resolved Layers identity is fixed in every option.

options.label: Split Evidence Desk
options.lineage: a wide source table paired with a persistent evidence pane
options.thesis: The exact CSV and the proof that it fits the model remain visible at the same time.
options.viewport: Raw rows dominate the left while source identity, contract fit, audit, and confirmation stay fixed on the right.
options.risk: The evidence pane can feel narrow on smaller laptop screens unless it collapses gracefully.

options.label: Dataset Dossier
options.lineage: a research dossier with source, columns, validation, and audit as one document
options.thesis: The selected file reads as a complete evidence object rather than an uploaded attachment.
options.viewport: A narrow project rail frames a strong file header, restrained evidence tabs, and a full source table.
options.risk: Tabs can hide relationships that the split view keeps simultaneously visible.

options.label: Evidence Ledger
options.lineage: a full-width scientific data ledger with an attached audit drawer
options.thesis: The uploaded rows remain the visual protagonist and every validation event is recorded beneath them.
options.viewport: The raw table fills the workspace while an open bottom drawer exposes identity, checks, and confirmation.
options.risk: The bottom drawer can reduce the number of visible rows and feel more technical than approachable.
